blocks.content: River capture, or stream piracy, occurs when a powerful stream with greater headward erosion breaches a drainage divide and diverts the waters of an adjacent river into its own channel.

rows: The energetic stream that breaches the divide through active headward erosion.
The sharp, right-angled bend where the stream water is diverted.
The abandoned, dry valley downstream of the capture point.
The remaining stream below the wind gap, too small for the valley it occupies.

items: Identify the signature landforms of river capture: Elbow of Capture, Wind Gap, and Misfit Stream.
Distinguish clearly between the Pirate Stream (captor) and the Misfit Stream (deprived lower course).
Himalayan river evolution examples, such as the historic capture of the ancient Saraswati River headwaters by the Yamuna, are frequently tested.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: River capture occurs when a stream with strong headward erosion breaches a drainage divide and diverts an adjacent stream.
The energetic capturing river is called the pirate stream, whereas the diverted stream is known as the captured stream.
Morphological evidence includes the elbow of capture, wind gap (dry valley), and misfit (underfit) stream.
Steep gradient, structural faults, and soft rocks accelerate headward erosion leading to stream piracy.
